newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish pension funds should up asset returns-OECD.
newsitem.headline: Finnish pension funds should up asset returns-OECD.

text.p: The Finnish pension funding system should be restructured to allow institutions to aim for a higher return on assets through more investments in shares and by allowing more investment overseas, the OECD said.
"Pension funds usually achieve much higher rates of return than are considered normal in Finland," the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development said in a report.
The report was originally scheduled for release on Monday but the embargo was lifted on Friday after information from the report was published ahead of schedule.
Pointing at nominal returns around 17.5 percent in the United Kingdom, it said such returns required "a much larger weight of shares in the funds' portfolio than currently adopted in Finland".

In 1996, shares accounted for 7.7 percent of Finnish employment pension funds' asset portfolios while bonds made up 42.9 percent, re-lending 21.3 percent and money market instruments 8.7 percent, the OECD said.

Before recent reforms of a highly-regulated system, the effects of which have not yet taken full effect, Finnish pension funds "had practically no alternative to investing in government bonds," it noted.
A two percentage-point rise in return on assets from an assumed real rate of return of three percent would double the financial assets available by the year 2030, OECD said.

But higher returns through more investment in shares could prove difficult. "The capitalisation of the Helsinki stock exchange appears to be too small to absorb the pension funds' resources despite the recent wave of privatisations," OECD said.
And funds were also constrained by European Union regulation stating that pension funds' holdings of foreign securities must not exceed a risk-adjusted 20 percent of their total portfolio.
This restriction would probably be lifted for investments in EMU countries when the single currency was established, it said.

The institutional setting of the Finnish pension fund system should also be changed to "strengthen the incentives for pension funds to become more active participants in international capital markets," OECD said.
